reviews.quote: This bargain laptop is no big deal — a dismal screen, subpar keyboard, outdated CPU and non-upgradeable 8GB of RAM.
The Vivobook Go 15 makes a solid, affordable everyday machine, with the OLED option a real standout at this price.

praises: 16GB LPDDR5 from the box keeps 30+ Chrome tabs and Teams smooth for everyday work
Fingerprint reader login at under $800 on sale — rare in this class
Wi-Fi 6E radio, unusual at this price and helpful on busy networks
Webcam privacy shutter and a real numpad in a 1.63 kg chassis
Silent and cool for browsing/office; the Mendocino chip barely warms up
complaints: Soldered LPDDR5 is a dead-end — what you buy is what you keep
Ryzen 5 40 is 4 threads of Zen 2: video editing and heavy Excel crawl
Regular $1,299.95 is far above what this hardware deserves; only the sale is real
Thin plastic Go chassis flexes more than the standard Vivobook 15
USB-C is data-only; barrel charging, no external monitor over USB-C

standouts: Fingerprint reader + Wi-Fi 6E + 16GB at $799.95 sale: best feature-density of the Go line
design_philosophy: The 'Go' tier trims the Vivobook 15 chassis to the cheapest build ASUS will stamp, then differentiates with features that photograph well on a spec sheet: 16GB LPDDR5, Wi-Fi 6E, and a fingerprint reader. The CPU — a 4-thread Zen 2 refresh — is the quiet compromise, making this a superb everyday machine for light users and a poor one for anyone who compiles, edits, or multitasks hard.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-vivobook.md). Platform-anchored on Ryzen 5 40 (Mendocino 4C/4T): same class as the Vivobook 16's 3501U but soldered RAM drops upgradability to 3.5; fingerprint and Wi-Fi 6E noted in sentiment, not scored separately.
